subsystems.name: Cold atom source
subsystems.role: produces a cloud of atoms cooled to microkelvin temperatures.

subsystems.name: Laser system
subsystems.role: cools, launches and manipulates the atoms with precise light pulses.

subsystems.name: Interferometer
subsystems.role: splits, redirects and recombines the atom wavepacket to measure gravity.

subsystems.name: Vibration isolation
subsystems.role: suppresses seismic noise that would otherwise swamp the gravity signal.

subsystems.name: Control and data system
subsystems.role: times the laser pulses and extracts the gravity value.

subsystems.name: Environmental housing
subsystems.role: keeps the sensor stable in field conditions.

buildSteps.title: Build the vacuum chamber
buildSteps.detail: Fabricate an ultra-high-vacuum chamber with optical access and magnetic shielding to host the atom cloud.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the laser system
buildSteps.detail: Set up frequency-stabilized lasers for cooling, state preparation and Raman transitions, and route them through optical fibres.

buildSteps.title: Load and cool atoms
buildSteps.detail: Release atoms from a source, trap them with magnetic fields and laser light, and cool them to a few microkelvin.

buildSteps.title: Launch and split the atoms
buildSteps.detail: Use laser pulses to launch the cloud upward and then place it in a superposition of two momentum states with a π/2 Raman pulse.

buildSteps.title: Apply interferometry sequence
buildSteps.detail: After a period of free fall, a π pulse redirects the states and a final π/2 pulse recombines them; the phase shift depends on gravity.

buildSteps.title: Detect and isolate vibrations
buildSteps.detail: Measure the population of each state by fluorescence, while seismometers and active stages cancel platform vibration.

buildSteps.title: Calibrate and package
buildSteps.detail: Convert the measured phase to acceleration or gravity gradient, then ruggedize the system for field deployment.

prerequisites.why: slows atoms to microkelvin temperatures, essential for long interferometry times.
demonstrated in laboratory gravimeters and gradiometers for decades.
field-ready systems need rugged, low-power lasers and optics.
seismic noise must be suppressed to reach useful gravity sensitivity.
some absolute gravimeters are sold, but gradiometers and mobile systems are still maturing.

pathway.milestone: laboratory and commercial absolute gravimeters used in geophysics
pathway.unlocks: precise monitoring of water, magma and subsurface density.

pathway.milestone: portable gravity gradiometers for field surveys
pathway.unlocks: faster, cheaper exploration for minerals and buried cavities.
large-area surveys of aquifers, ore bodies and underground structures.

pathway.milestone: underwater gravity gradiometry for submerged-object detection
pathway.unlocks: a potential route to detecting vessels or tunnels, though still largely research.
